title: The Clean Energy-Health-Development Dividend
subtitle: How Energy Transition Pathways Can Simultaneously Improve Environmental Quality, Public Health, and Economic Performance
dek: Quantifies how clean-energy transition pathways—coal-to-solar grids, electric mobility, and clean cooking—simultaneously slash lethal PM2.5 air pollution, save millions of lives, and boost emerging-economy labor productivity through 2050.
abstract: Energy policy, environmental regulation, and public health have traditionally been budgeted and governed in separate ministerial silos—obscuring one of the highest-return synergies in modern development economics. Every year, fossil-fuel combustion and household solid-biomass smoke generate more than 8 million premature deaths worldwide, strip years off life expectancy across Asia and Africa, depress factory and outdoor worker output, and impose trillions of dollars in preventable healthcare and productivity losses. Anchored to 10 live World Bank World Development Indicators across 24 economies and regional aggregates and 24 peer-reviewed studies in epidemiology, labor economics, and energy-systems modeling, this monograph quantifies the integrated Clean Energy-Health-Development Dividend.

Live 2024–2025 WDI baselines expose an acute environmental-health divide: Bangladesh (69.3 ug/m3), Nigeria (65.7 ug/m3), and India (54.1 ug/m3) endure ambient PM2.5 concentrations 10 to 14 times above World Health Organization guidelines, while clean-cooking access lags at just 7.0% in Ethiopia, 15.6% in low-income economies, and 22.9% in Sub-Saharan Africa (where under-5 mortality remains 71.2 per 1,000 live births versus 5.1 in high-income nations). Modeling an integrated clean-energy pathway combining utility solar-plus-storage coal displacement, urban e-mobility, universal clean cooking, and solarized health clinics, this study projects a cumulative 2026–2050 EMDE Clean Energy-Health-Development Dividend of USD 38 trillion to USD 64 trillion (central: USD 51.0 trillion, constant 2025 USD; 3% NPV: USD 30.2 trillion)—demonstrating that local health and productivity co-benefits alone exceed transition capital costs by 2x to 4x.
findings: Documents the live 2024–2025 air-quality and clean-cooking divide across 10 WDI indicators (PM2.5 up to 69.3 ug/m3; clean cooking at 15.6% in LICs vs. 99.5% in HICs).
Synthesizes causal evidence proving that local health co-benefits (USD 50–380/tCO2) and clean-air worker productivity gains exceed clean-energy mitigation costs by 2x–4x.
Projects a cumulative 2026–2050 EMDE Clean Energy-Health-Development Dividend of USD 38T–64T (central: USD 51.0T; 3% NPV: USD 30.2T) across five transmission channels.
keywords: clean cooking transition and child survival
method: Empirical synthesis using verified World Bank WDI and international datasets, peer-reviewed literature, H Heuristics Cross-System Spillover (2nd–4th order) mapping, maladaptation guardrails, and quantitative 2050 polycrisis scenarios.
